speaker: Doctor
text: I see a historical note suggesting Tuberculosis, but I need to evaluate this based on your current symptoms and findings. Can you tell me how long you have been experiencing these fatigue, abdominal pain, night sweats, weight loss, and enlarged supraclavicular lymph nodes?

speaker: Patient
text: I have been feeling very tired and have had worsening abdominal pain for about four weeks. I have also had drenching night sweats and lost about twelve pounds.

speaker: Doctor
text: The duration of four weeks with significant weight loss and night sweats is concerning. To evaluate the abdominal pain and lymphadenopathy, can you describe the exact location of your pain and if you have any history of recent travel or contact with someone who has an infectious disease? REQUEST TEST: CBC with differential, ESR, and LDH.

speaker: Measurement
text: RESULTS: CBC with differential: WBC - Elevated, Hemoglobin - Slightly Decreased, Platelets - Normal; Lactate Dehydrogenase (LDH) - Elevated. ESR: Not available.

speaker: Doctor
text: The lab results show elevated white blood cells and LDH with mild anemia, which supports an active proliferative or inflammatory process like lymphoma. Given your B symptoms and supraclavicular nodes, have you noticed any pain in the lymph nodes, and do you have a fever or a history of smoking? REQUEST IMAGES: Chest_X-Ray, Abdominal_US.

speaker: Patient
text: I noticed swelling in my neck over the last few days. It does not hurt, but it feels enlarged and fixed.

speaker: Doctor
text: The description of a "fixed" and painless supraclavicular node is highly concerning for malignancy. Have you noticed any changes in your bowel habits, such as constipation, diarrhea, or blood in your stool? REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen/Pelvis.

speaker: Patient
text: I also feel fullness in my abdomen and my clothes feel tighter. I do not have cough or recent travel.

speaker: Doctor
text: The sensation of abdominal fullness with tighter clothing suggests hepatosplenomegaly or significant lymphadenopathy. Have you noticed any jaundice, easy bruising, or bleeding gums? REQUEST IMAGES: CT Abdomen/Pelvis with contrast.

speaker: Patient
text: I have smoked about one pack a day for many years, and I drink socially. The abdominal discomfort and fatigue have both been getting worse.

speaker: Doctor
text: The history of long-term heavy smoking significantly increases your risk for malignancies, including lung cancer with mediastinal involvement or lymphoma. Given your "fixed" supraclavicular node, significant weight loss, night sweats, and abdominal fullness, we must proceed immediately to imaging to define the extent of the disease. DIAGNOSIS READY: Non-Hodgkin Lymphoma (suspect Diffuse Large B-Cell Lymphoma) or Metastatic Lung Cancer.
